title: BOSS: Blocking algorithm for optimizing shuttling scheduling in Ion Trap
problem: Shuttling operations in ion trap quantum computers cause significant fidelity loss and elongated execution times, particularly as circuit sizes grow to 4000+ two-qubit gates across 64-78 qubits.
motivation: Ion traps offer high-fidelity gates, long coherence times, and extensive connectivity, but their scalability is bottlenecked by shuttling overhead, which degrades both fidelity and throughput.
method: BOSS groups quantum operations (the instructions given to qubits) into blocks to minimize how many times ions need to be shuttled (moved) across the trap. By batching related operations together, the algorithm reduces the total shuttling overhead that would otherwise happen between every operation. It uses realistic experimental conditions, including sympathetic cooling (a technique where one cooled ion helps cool others nearby), to predict execution time and fidelity more accurately. Testing covers circuits with 4000+ two-qubit gates across 64-78 qubits.
key_novelty: BOSS cuts shuttling operations by up to 96.1% by grouping quantum operations based on which qubits they use, taking advantage of the fact that related operations often cluster on nearby qubits.
contributions: Blocking algorithm (BOSS) for shuttling scheduling that reduces shuttle operations by up to 96.1%
Integration of realistic sympathetic cooling parameters for higher-fidelity simulation and accurate execution time estimates
Validation on circuits with up to 4000+ two-qubit gates and 64-78 qubits

metrics.accuracy: fidelity loss reduction via sympathetic cooling simulation

limitations: Evaluated on simulated environments; real-hardware validation at full scale not demonstrated.
primary_theme: shuttling scheduling optimization for ion trap quantum computers
